# Refined Cost Segregation

> Documentary, cost-library-based, ATG-aligned cost segregation studies, reviewed by a licensed tax professional, for 1-4 unit residential property, including short-term rentals (STR) and long-term rentals (LTR). Serves clients across the United States. No site visits required; the methodology is documentary, working from closing statements, photos, and structured intake.

## About

Refined Cost Segregation is a residential-specialty cost segregation firm built by tax and real estate professionals. Every study is reviewed and signed off by a qualified licensed tax professional.

The firm exists to make defensible, audit-ready cost segregation accessible to the 1-4 unit residential investor market that traditional commercial cost-seg firms serve poorly or charge disproportionately for. Pricing is a transparent, formula-based fixed fee, quoted per property from the intake form or a call rather than published. Optional Audit Support is available in Basic (first-claim year, exams within 3 years) and Extended (any affected year, exams within 10 years) levels. Over 12 units are quoted individually.

## Key facts (current as of 2026)

- 100% bonus depreciation was restored for property acquired (contract signed) and placed in service after January 19, 2025, by the One Big Beautiful Bill (OBBB), signed mid-2025. No scheduled sunset.
- A typical residential cost segregation study reclassifies 20-35% of depreciable basis into 5-, 7-, and 15-year property; short-term rentals often land in the upper part of that range.
- For STRs with an average customer-use period of 7 days or less, IRS Treasury Regulation §1.469-1T(e)(3) treats the activity as a non-rental trade or business. Material participation (any of the IRS's 7 tests) makes the resulting losses non-passive and usable against W-2 income.
- Deliverables: the report PDF, a per-asset fixed-asset schedule (CSV), and a one-page CPA implementation letter, delivered by email within 5-10 business days of a complete questionnaire.
- Process: instant estimate and flat fee shown before payment → Stripe checkout → 10–15 minute property questionnaire → automated working-file build → human reviewer + QC → licensed-professional sign-off → delivery.
- Services: residential (1-4 unit) studies, short-term-rental studies, optional Audit Support (Basic 3-year / Extended 10-year), and a CPA partner program. Study pricing is quoted per property (not published).

## Methodology and language

- "Audit-ready, ATG-aligned, reviewed by a licensed tax professional," never "audit-proof," which overpromises and isn't accurate.
- Documentary, cost-library-based methodology, prepared to the IRS Cost Segregation Audit Techniques Guide.
- Documentary process; no site visits required for 1-4 unit residential.
- Always works alongside the client's CPA, never replaces or poaches.

Here's the realistic cost segregation timeline to get the property placed in service, the study engaged, and the deduction on this year's return before December 31.
- [Cost segregation and the QBI deduction: does it shrink your Section 199A write-off?](https://www.refinedcostseg.com/journal/cost-segregation-qbi-deduction.html): Accelerating depreciation with a cost segregation study can push a rental's QBI toward zero or negative. Here's how the Section 199A interaction actually works, with a worked example.
- [Cost segregation on a property with an ADU](https://www.refinedcostseg.com/journal/cost-segregation-adu.html): An ADU is its own asset for depreciation purposes, not a slice of the main house. How the acquisition-date rule works for a self-built accessory dwelling unit, what a study finds inside one, and a worked $210K example.
- [Bonus depreciation on a used rental property](https://www.refinedcostseg.com/journal/bonus-depreciation-used-property.html): Bonus depreciation isn't just for new construction. A used residential rental bought from an unrelated seller qualifies for 100% bonus depreciation on its short-life components. Here's the acquisition rule, the two real disqualifiers, and a worked $480K example.
- [Is cost segregation worth it on a smaller rental?](https://www.refinedcostseg.com/journal/is-cost-segregation-worth-it-small-rental.html): There is no minimum property value for cost segregation. Here is what actually decides whether a study is worth it on a smaller, lower-priced residential rental, with a worked $235K example.
- [Cost segregation when you house hack](https://www.refinedcostseg.com/journal/cost-segregation-house-hacking.html): You bought a 2-4 unit, live in one, and rent the rest. The unit you live in isn't depreciable, but cost segregation still accelerates the rental share, and it can qualify for 100% bonus depreciation.
- [Cost segregation on inherited property](https://www.refinedcostseg.com/journal/cost-segregation-inherited-property.html): You inherited a rental and got a stepped-up basis at fair market value. A cost segregation study still accelerates it, but here's why bonus depreciation usually won't apply to inherited property.
- [Cost segregation on a BRRRR or renovation](https://www.refinedcostseg.com/journal/cost-segregation-brrrr-renovation.html): Finished a BRRRR or gut renovation on a rental? Your capitalized rehab dollars are all depreciable building basis, with no land to strip out, and they skew toward the short-life property a cost segregation study can accelerate into year one. A worked $150K example.
- [Cost segregation in an LLC or partnership](https://www.refinedcostseg.com/journal/cost-segregation-llc-partnership.html): Does holding your rental in an LLC change your cost segregation deduction? The entity doesn't resize the write-off, basis is basis, but a partnership splits it across K-1s and each owner's participation decides who can use it. A worked $600K example.
- [Cost segregation with a mortgage on your rental](https://www.refinedcostseg.com/journal/cost-segregation-with-a-mortgage.html): You put 20% down and the bank owns the rest, so is a cost segregation study even worth it? Your deduction follows the building's basis, not your down payment or equity. Why leverage doesn't shrink the write-off, with a worked $500K example.
- [Cost segregation before the extension deadline](https://www.refinedcostseg.com/journal/cost-segregation-extension-deadline.html): Filed an extension on your 2025 return? Until it's filed, a cost segregation study can still land the full first-year deduction on it. The September 15 and October 15 runway, with a worked $475K example.
- [Cost segregation on new construction](https://www.refinedcostseg.com/journal/cost-segregation-new-construction.html): Can you run a cost segregation study on a rental you built rather than bought? Yes, and new construction is often the cleanest study there is. How the actual cost records help, how 100% bonus depreciation applies, and a worked $480K example.
- [Cost segregation and the partial disposition election](https://www.refinedcostseg.com/journal/cost-segregation-partial-disposition-election.html): When you renovate a rental and rip out the old roof, HVAC, or kitchen, a partial disposition election lets you write off its remaining basis as a loss. How cost segregation makes it possible, with a worked example.
- [Does your state follow federal bonus depreciation?](https://www.refinedcostseg.com/journal/state-bonus-depreciation-conformity.html): Federal bonus depreciation gives a full year-one write-off, but many states decouple and add it back. Here's what state conformity means for your cost segregation deduction, with a worked $500K example.
- [Cost segregation on a mid-term rental](https://www.refinedcostseg.com/journal/mid-term-rental-cost-segregation.html): A mid-term (30+ day) rental reclassifies like a furnished STR, but the 30-day guest fails the seven-day test, so the loss is passive. What a cost seg study delivers on an MTR, and a worked $520K example.
- [Cost segregation on a vacation home you use yourself](https://www.refinedcostseg.com/journal/vacation-home-cost-segregation-personal-use.html): Using your rental yourself? Personal-use days can cap your write-off under Section 280A. How the 14-day/10% rule changes cost segregation, with a worked $600K example.
- [What a cost segregation study reclassifies: 5-, 7-, and 15-year property](https://www.refinedcostseg.com/journal/what-cost-segregation-reclassifies-5-7-15-year-property.html): Residential rentals depreciate over 27.5 years. A cost segregation study moves qualifying components into 5-, 7-, and 15-year buckets. Exactly what reclassifies, what stays, and a worked $500K example.
- [Land value allocation and cost segregation](https://www.refinedcostseg.com/journal/land-value-allocation-cost-segregation.html): Land isn't depreciable, so how you split a purchase price between land and building sets the ceiling on every deduction a cost segregation study can produce. Why a high land allocation costs you, and how to support a defensible one, with a worked example.
- [Cost segregation after a 1031 exchange](https://www.refinedcostseg.com/journal/cost-segregation-1031-exchange.html): A 1031 exchange splits your replacement property into carryover basis and excess basis. Only one side is bonus-eligible. Here's how cost segregation works after a like-kind exchange, with a worked example.
- [Converting a home to a rental: cost segregation and bonus depreciation](https://www.refinedcostseg.com/journal/converting-primary-residence-to-rental-cost-segregation.html): Converting a former home to a rental? Cost segregation still accelerates your depreciation, but the restored 100% bonus usually won't apply. Here's why, with the numbers.
- [Cost segregation for passive investors: what happens to the losses](https://www.refinedcostseg.com/journal/cost-segregation-passive-losses.html): No REPS, no STR loophole? Cost segregation losses you can't deduct this year aren't lost. They're suspended, they offset passive income, and they release in full when you sell. A worked $450K example.
- [Real estate professional status: what it unlocks](https://www.refinedcostseg.com/journal/real-estate-professional-status-cost-segregation.html): Real estate professional status makes rental losses non-passive, which is what lets a cost segregation deduction offset W-2 income. The two tests, a worked $640K example, and the documentation that holds up.

How §1245 ordinary recapture and unrecaptured §1250 gain actually work, with a worked $525K example.

The timing math, when waiting makes sense, and how to decide.
- [Bonus depreciation vs. Section 179 for residential rentals](https://www.refinedcostseg.com/journal/bonus-depreciation-vs-section-179-residential-rentals.html): Bonus depreciation and Section 179 both expense rental assets up front, but only one can create a loss. The difference that decides which fits your residential rental, with a worked $92K example.

The five most-missed, with a worked example.
